Hi Alice — great to hear, glad the demo landed well.

Sending our current hosted API rate card (attached) and an initial note on streaming billing below — happy to hop on a short call if the vendor committee wants to walk through examples.

Quick summary (baseline):
- Hosted API: billed per generated token. For streaming generations we bill tokens as they are emitted by the service (server-side).
- Baseline fees: no per-request flat fee for standard text generations; embeddings and specialized routes have separate units (see attached rate card).
- Discounting: standard tiered discounts applied on committed monthly/annual spend. Typical early-stage ARR discount (for < $250k) is 5–10% on list; higher tiers available with commitments.

Streaming billing notes (initial):
- Tokens are metered and billed when the server commits them to the response stream. If a client disconnects after N tokens were emitted, those N tokens are counted.
- Retries: if a later retry causes the service to re-emit the same tokens (duplication), we attempt server-side dedup where possible — short replays within a 30s reconnection window are deduped. Outside that window duplicate tokens may be billed.
- Partial generations resumed: if we can resume from a preserved KV cache and continue, only newly generated tokens are billed. If the system restarts the generation path and replays, billing reflects emitted tokens.

I'll put Dev on this thread to confirm the exact dedup window and whether we can commit to a one-time credit in tight outage cases. Attaching: rate_card_v1.pdf for your committee.

Best,

Karthik — thanks for the loop. Dev and I discussed; here's the official guidance you can send to Horizon and keep in the contract appendix. Please include the attached billing_policy_streaming_v2.pdf when you send.

Official streaming billing guidance (approved):
- Metering point: billing is per generated token, recorded at the moment the server emits the token to the response pipeline. Emitted tokens appear in the billing export as 'generated_token' lines with timestamp and request_id.
- Partial/disconnects: tokens already emitted before a disconnect are billable. If a client reconnects and resumes within the 30-second deduplication window, our runtime attempts to deduplicate repeated emissions tied to the same request_id and session token; duplicated emissions within that window are not billed twice.
- Retries that intentionally re-run a request (new request_id): these are treated as separate billable runs. If Horizon wants retry resilience without double billing, recommend using our client SDK helpers that persist a resume token and perform graceful reconnects (see SDK section in attached doc).
- Long streams: for extremely long/indefinite streams we recommend checkpointing at logical boundaries and using the streaming 'resume' API that persists KV cache server-side; this minimizes rework and duplicate generation.
- Credits: we will evaluate verified overbilling incidents on a case-by-case basis. For first-time onboarding incidents we allow a one-time pro-rated goodwill credit up to 5% of the first invoice, provided the cause is on the Redwood side (e.g., confirmed runtime bug or outage). Routine client-side retries or misconfiguration are not eligible.

Concrete examples to include in your reply to Horizon:
1) Simple disconnect
   - Start generation: server emits 120 tokens, connection drops. Horizon reconnects and requests to resume; server resumes and emits additional 20 tokens = 140 total. Billing: 140 tokens billed (120 before drop + 20 after resume).
2) Duplicate replay within dedup window
   - Client experiences transient duplicate frames; runtime detects same request_id and repeats first 60 tokens within 15s. Runtime dedupes those 60 tokens and bills only unique tokens emitted.
3) Explicit retry as new request_id
   - Client retries intentionally (new request_id) and the service replays first 60 tokens then emits 80 new tokens. Billing: charged for all tokens emitted across both request_ids (duplicates billed) unless a support-reviewed billing adjustment is approved.

Please attach the billing_policy_streaming_v2.pdf and the Horizon_Quote_DEAL-2026-0042.pdf if you mention discounts in the vendor committee. Offer language: "Redwood will extend a 7.5% introductory usage discount on the first 6 months for Horizon if you sign a 9-month pilot commitment of >= $120k." That's approved for you to offer.

Let me know once you send the final note and I'll make sure finance flags any requested credits.
